post.originalText:
I gave Opus 5.5 one brief: make a 12-minute documentary on Elon Musk, using real footage, with a narrator in the Attenborough register, and make something people actually feel. Not a fact montage.

It did the rest: found and downloaded ~80 clips from 60 Minutes, NASA, SpaceX webcasts, and a 2008 documentary; transcribed all of them so it could cut on exact words; designed an original narrator voice from a text description, with no voice cloning; and even built a measurable test for “sounds human” when it realized it couldn’t hear.

It scored the film with Satie, Dvořák, Beethoven, Elgar, and Holst, then cut the footage to the music.

My job was to watch each cut and tell it what didn’t land. Four rounds.

The first version was honestly bad. By the fourth, it was finding flash frames I’d missed and fixing them across the entire film.

All local tools 👇

inputs.description: Around 80 historical video clips downloaded from 60 Minutes, CBS, Bloomberg, NASA, SpaceX, and documentaries
inputs.evidence: found and downloaded ~80 clips from 60 Minutes, NASA, SpaceX webcasts, and a 2008 documentary

inputs.description: Public domain classical music recordings (Satie, Dvořák, Beethoven 7, Elgar, Holst)
inputs.evidence: Wikimedia Commons API: public-domain recordings of Satie, Dvořák (Largo and finale), Elgar's Nimrod and Holst's Jupiter

inputs.description: Voice timbre WAV reference and emotion audio clips for TTS transfer
inputs.evidence: The file is vo/refs/spk_grandfather.wav... Tender lines... use a clip of Kimbal speaking about his brother.

tools.name: ffmpeg & Pillow & Python
tools.role: Timeline assembly, scene detection, visual overlays, audio mixing, and video rendering
tools.evidence: ffmpeg: all cutting, cropping, color, overlays, the music ducking under voices, and the -16 LUFS master; Pillow: chapter cards, lower-third captions and title cards

tools.name: librosa
tools.role: Audio analysis for take selection and emotional arc pacing
tools.evidence: librosa: pitch-range, pause and loudness analysis, used to pick the most human-sounding narration takes

tools.name: mlx-whisper
tools.role: Clip transcription and word-level timestamp generation
tools.evidence: mlx-whisper (large-v3-turbo): transcribed every clip with word-level timestamps, so every bite is cut on exact words

tools.name: VoiceStudio (IndexTTS 2.5 / VoxCPM2)
tools.role: Voice generation and emotive TTS delivery synthesis
tools.evidence: The narrator is IndexTTS 2.5, one of the engines in VoiceStudio... Timbre comes from the VoxCPM2 voice, delivery from real human emotion references

tools.name: yt-dlp & NASA Image/Video API & Internet Archive
tools.evidence: yt-dlp: downloaded the YouTube clips... NASA Image and Video Library API... Internet Archive
